contexts.text: This gave rise to a suspicion that he had committed some murder in the life of the body. SE 1260.
So that no one could suspect them... SE 1491.
So that the husband has no suspicion. SE 4082.
They who belong to this province (of the infundibulum of the brain) are prone to suspicions, impatient, etc. SE 915.
An unjust jealousy exists with those who are suspicious by nature...

A suspicious fancy, if long fed, introduces the mind into Societies of like Spirits... A failing of the manly powers... causes that the mind cannot be elevated from its suspicious [fancies]. Explained.
(The renal Spirits) began, in their usual way, to suspect evils of them...
So that there should be no suspicion that it was from them.
Of whom men had never suspected such a thing (while they were in the body). SE 2883.
A child came... whom I could not suspect...
Whom I could not suspect of such a thing.
